summary: Former Six Rivers NF tower site in Del Norte County; construction and removal dates unknown; a June 2020 hiker found only rocks, metal and chimney pieces.

facts.design: Short, open timber tower with a partial catwalk; FFLOS says it appears to follow a USFS R1 cabin plan
facts.status_note: Former lookout site; in June 2020 a hiker found only a square of loose rocks strewn with metal and flattened chimney pieces; no source describes a standing tower

access.note: Trailhead on FS 15 (G-O Road) and the trail lies in the Smith River National Recreation Area; the 2020 summit route was faint and no source says whether it is maintained or open

visit.trail_note: Summit Valley Trail: South Fork Road from Hwy 199 (about 13.7 miles), then FS 15 (G-O Road) about 15 miles to the trailhead; 1.5 miles one way to the valley meadow; rated moderate, downhill; the 2020 route to the summit used cairns and was hard to follow near the top

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the location as Siskiyou National Forest but the administering unit as Six Rivers National Forest; the Forest Lookouts page and the 1940 plan also name the Siskiyou. The Smith River Alliance places the trailhead in the Six Rivers National Forest. The story does not name a forest.

sources.title: South Siskiyou: Summit Valley Lookout and back along South Fork Smith River

notes_for_editor: The brief's status 'gone' is supported only indirectly: the register lists it as a former site with unknown removal date, and the June 2020 blog describes rocks and metal, not a tower. No source gives a build or removal year. Elevation 1,507 m (4,944 ft) and coordinates match the register. The brief's kind 'tower' matches the register's description. The Forest Service recreation listing (recid=11468) read this session is a general forest page with no Summit Valley entry, so it is not cited. The 2020 blog is a personal hiking account and is the only description of the site today; the story says so by describing only what it found. Access is marked public on the strength of the trailhead and NRA trail description, not a closure notice; the summit route's status is unverified. Two WebSearch calls and four distinct page reads (register, Forest Lookouts, Smith River Alliance, blog) were used, with the forest recreation page as a fifth read that yielded no site data.
